name: Instant adhesive, medium-low viscosity
summary: EPOBOND-FAST CX-401 is a very fast curing, medium-low viscosity modified ethyl cyanoacrylate adhesive. It is suitable for the bonding of a very wide range of materials, including acidic surfaces and some porous ones, where rapid bonding times are required.
notes: Viscosity: cone and plate rheometer, controlled stress
Tensile strength: ISO 6922
Fixture time: depending on substrates and application conditions
sections: EPOBOND-FAST CX-401 is especially formulated for instant bonding of paper, leather, wood, plastics, rubbers, metals and other common substrates. CX-401 will be used in many markets such as assembly of plastic and rubber parts, shoe manufacture and repair, luggage manufacturing, sports equipment manufacture, the electrical and electronic device industry, medical devices, maintenance and repair and many others. Although CX-401 has a degree of gap filling ability, it is generally recommended for use on close-fitting parts and fairly smooth, even surfaces.
Steel at two minutes 50% of final strength

Bond speed is very fast so ensure that parts are properly aligned before bonding. Activator AX40 may be required if there are gaps or porous surfaces. Some plastics may require application of AP50 Primer.

Ensure parts are clean, dry and free from oil and grease. Product is normally hand applied from the bottle. Apply sparingly to one surface and press parts firmly together until handling strength is achieved. As a general rule, as little cyanoacrylate as possible should be used - over application will result in slow cure speed and lower bond strength. Please contact your EPOBOND representative for further advice on dispensing solutions.

EPOBOND-FAST cyanoacrylates give best results on close fitting parts. The product should be applied in a very thin line in order to ensure rapid polymerisation and a strong bond. Excessive bond gaps will result in slower cure speeds.

The speed of cure of cyanoacrylates varies according to the substrates to be bonded. Acidic surfaces such as leather and paper have longer cure times than most plastics and rubbers. Some plastics such as polyethylene, polypropylene and PTFE require the use of AP50 Primer.

EPOBOND-FAST ethyl cyanoacrylate adhesives are suitable for use at temperatures up to 80°C. At 80°C the bond will be approximately 70% of the strength at 21°C. The bond strength at 100°C is approximately 50% of full strength at 21°C.

EPOBOND-FAST cyanoacrylates retain over 90% of their strength when heated to 100°C for 90 days and then tested at 21°C. Heating the bond to 120°C and then testing at 21°C gives bond strength of approximately 50% of initial strength.

EPOBOND-FAST cyanoacrylates exhibit excellent chemical resistance to most oils and solvents including motor oil, leaded petrol, ethanol, propanol and freon. Cyanoacrylates are not resistant to high levels of moisture or humidity over time.
Store in a cool area out of direct sunlight. Refrigeration to 5°C gives optimum storage stability.

name: Threadlocker, low strength (Screwlock)
summary: EPOBOND-LOCK TL-1222 Screwlock is a low strength, thixotropic anaerobic threadlocker. The low removal torque allows easy disassembly yet provides maximum vibration and shock resistance for threaded parts. Low strength, easy disassembly, 50 gm net.
notes: Viscosity: Brookfield RVT spindle 2, 2.5 rpm
Viscosity, second method: Brookfield RVT spindle 2
Torque: on M10 black oxide steel bolt and M10 bright steel nut
Fixture time: ISO 10964
sections: EPOBOND-LOCK TL-1222 is formulated to prevent vibration loosening and to seal against leaks through threaded components. The low removal torque makes TL-1222 especially suitable for use on small threaded parts (<6mmø) and where regular disassembly is envisaged. TL-1222 is ideal for small set screws and hex and slot driven components, including keyed fasteners. The low strength allows disassembly without stripping the heads off screws or bolts, so TL-1222 is particularly recommended for use on softer, non-ferrous metals, e.g. brass.

Suitable for small screws and screws with small heads, diameters or lengths where frequent disassembly and re-assembly is needed, e.g. switches, speed-adjusting knobs and tools on machines, and for weak metals such as aluminium and brass that may break on disassembly.
Typical curing speed as % of final strength:
TL-1222 is suitable for low strength applications that require small to medium gap filling.

Ensure parts are clean, dry and free from oil and grease. Apply adhesive to all the engaged area. Assemble parts and allow to cure. Wipe excess adhesive from outside of joint. Product is normally hand applied from the bottle or tube. Dispensing systems are available for high volume assembly applications. Please contact your EPOBOND representative for further advice on dispensing solutions.
All figures relating to cure speed are tested at 21°C. Lower temperatures will result in slower cure. Heating the assembled parts accelerates the curing process.
Activator AX 40 should be used when the temperature is less than 5°C.

Cure speed and strength vary according to the substrates. When used on mild steel and brass components anaerobic adhesives will reach full strength more rapidly than more inert materials such as stainless steel and zinc dichromate. EPOBOND-LOCK AX 40 activator may be used to accelerate cure speed. Anaerobic adhesives only cure in the absence of air and with metal part activation.

The size of the bond gap greatly affects the speed of cure of anaerobic adhesives. The larger the gap between the mating surfaces, the slower the cure speed. Maximum recommended gap for TL-1222 is 0.25mm, which will give approximately the cure schedule as detailed in the properties table.
EPOBOND-LOCK TL-1222 is suitable for use at temperatures up to 150°C. At 130°C the bond strength will be ~20% of the strength at 21°C.
EPOBOND-LOCK anaerobics retain over 90% of full strength when heated to 100°C for 90 days, then cooled and tested at 21°C.

EPOBOND-LOCK anaerobics exhibit excellent chemical resistance to most oils and solvents including motor oil, leaded petrol, brake fluid, acetone, ethanol, propanol and water. Anaerobic adhesives and sealants are not recommended for use in pure oxygen or chlorine lines.

TL-1222 is not recommended on certain plastics as stress cracking can sometimes result. Some anti corrosion chemicals inhibit the cure system in this type of anaerobic. Trials are recommended to establish whether cleaning of the parts is necessary.
AX 40 Activator may be required on plated parts.
Optimal storage conditions are between 8°C and 21°C. Storage outside this temperature range can adversely affect product properties and affect the stated shelf life.

The thixotropic nature of the product prevents run off, dripping and migration after assembly. TL-1243 is typically used on mounting bolts, housing screws, etc. TL-1243 will help prevent the corrosion of assembled parts.
Also suitable for pump and gearbox bolts and motor-base bolts, for stainless steel, for parts contaminated with oils, and wherever disassembly with hand tools is needed for service and maintenance.

name: Threadlocker, high strength, permanent
summary: EPOBOND-LOCK TL-1270 is a single component, high strength (permanent) anaerobic thread locking compound. TL-1270 cures when confined in the absence of air between close fitting metal surfaces. High strength, permanent, 50 gm net.
notes: Viscosity: Brookfield LVF spindle 2, 2.5 rpm
Torque: on M10 black oxide steel bolt and M10 bright steel nut
Fixture time: ISO 10964
sections: EPOBOND-LOCK TL-1270 is formulated to lock metal fasteners and thus prevent vibration loosening and leakage through the threads. TL-1270 is particularly suitable for larger threaded fasteners, e.g. studs and all applications where maximum strength is needed. TL-1270 prevents corrosion of assembled parts.

Also suitable for stainless steel and for surfaces with protective coatings such as zinc that do not need frequent disassembly, and recommended for permanent fastening of motor-shaft bolts and engine parts.
Typical curing speed as % of final strength:
TL-1270 is suitable for most standard diameter, medium to coarse-threaded screws, nuts and bolts.

Ensure parts are clean, dry and free from oil and grease. Apply adhesive to all the engaged area. Assemble parts and allow to cure. Wipe excess adhesive from outside of joint. Product is normally hand applied from the bottle or tube. Dispensing systems are available for high volume assembly applications. Please contact your EPOBOND representative for further advice on dispensing solutions.
All figures relating to cure speed are tested at 21°C. Lower temperatures will result in slower cure. Heating the assembled parts accelerates the curing process.
Activator AX 40 should be used when the temperature is low.

Cure speed and strength vary according to the substrates. When used on mild steel and brass components anaerobic adhesives will reach full strength more rapidly than more inert materials such as stainless steel and zinc dichromate. EPOBOND-LOCK AX 40 activator may be used to accelerate cure speed. Anaerobic adhesives only cure in the absence of air and with metal part activation.

The size of the bond gap greatly affects the speed of cure of anaerobic adhesives. The larger the gap between the mating surfaces, the slower the cure speed. Maximum recommended gap for TL-1270 is 0.20mm, which will give approximately the cure schedule as detailed in the properties table.
EPOBOND-LOCK TL-1270 is suitable for use at temperatures up to 150°C. At 130°C the bond strength will be ~50% of the strength at 21°C.
EPOBOND-LOCK anaerobics retain over 90% of full strength when heated to 100°C for 90 days, then cooled and tested at 21°C.

EPOBOND-LOCK anaerobics exhibit excellent chemical resistance to most oils and solvents including motor oil, leaded petrol, brake fluid, acetone, ethanol, propanol and water. Anaerobic adhesives and sealants are not recommended for use in pure oxygen or chlorine lines.

TL-1270 is not recommended on certain plastics as stress cracking can sometimes result. Some anti corrosion chemicals inhibit the cure system in this type of anaerobic. Trials are recommended to establish whether cleaning of the parts is necessary.
AX 40 Activator may be required on plated parts.
Optimal storage conditions are between 8°C and 21°C. Storage outside this temperature range can adversely affect product properties and affect the stated shelf life.

Viscosity, second method: Brookfield RVT 'T'-spindle D, 20 rpm
Torque: on M10 black oxide steel bolt and M10 bright steel nut
sections: EPOBOND TS-1565 is formulated to lock and seal medium to coarse straight and tapered pipe threads on pipes Ø15mm to Ø80mm. TS-1565 prevents vibration loosening and leakage through the pipe threads. TS-1565 gives low strength break and prevail torque on assembled joints, thus enabling easier disassembly and servicing, which is further helped by the lubricity of TS-1565.
TS-1565 gives an almost instant low pressure seal (up to 2 Bar after 20 mins) and when fully cured will seal up to the bursting pressure of the pipe (e.g. 10,000 psi).
Gives controlled strength so that it prevents loosening or leakage caused by vibrations, with 100% leak prevention. Assembly and disassembly can be done with ordinary hand tools for maintenance.
Typical curing speed as % of final strength:

TS-1565 is suitable for most straight and tapered pipe threads of medium to coarse pitch, from Ø15mm to Ø80mm pipe. TS-1565 will not cure outside the joint and is virtually non-fouling in most types of pipe systems.

Ensure parts are clean, dry and free from oil and grease. Apply adhesive to all engaged threads, although to minimise excess adhesive inside the joint, apply adhesive only to the male part, leaving the first two threads clear. The size of the bond gap greatly affects the speed of cure of anaerobic adhesives. The larger the gap between the mating surfaces, the slower the cure speed. Maximum recommended gap for TS-1565 is 0.50mm.
EPOBOND TS-1565 is suitable for use at temperatures up to 150°C. At 150°C the bond strength will be ~30% of the strength at 21°C.
EPOBOND anaerobics retain ~85% of full strength when heated to 100°C for 90 days, then cooled and tested at 21°C.

EPOBOND anaerobics exhibit excellent chemical resistance to most oils and solvents including motor oil, leaded petrol, brake fluid, acetone, ethanol, propanol and water. Anaerobic adhesives and sealants are not recommended for use in pure oxygen or chlorine lines.

TS-1565 is not recommended on certain plastics as stress cracking can sometimes result. Some anti corrosion chemicals inhibit the cure system in this type of anaerobic. Trials are recommended to establish whether cleaning of the parts is necessary.

Wipe excess adhesive from outside of joint. If the temperature is less than 5°C AX-40 activator should be used. Product is normally hand applied from the bottle. Dispensing systems are available for high volume assembly applications. Please contact your EPOBOND representative for further advice on dispensing solutions.

Where speed of cure is too slow or the bond gap is very large, EPOBOND AX-40 Anaerobic Activator may be used to accelerate cure speed. The use of an accelerator may reduce bond strength by up to 30%. EPOBOND recommends testing on the parts to measure the effect.

The size of the bond gap greatly affects the speed of cure of anaerobic adhesives. The larger the gap between the mating surfaces, the slower the cure speed. Maximum recommended gap for GA-1574 is 0.35mm.
All figures relating to cure speed are tested at 21°C. Lower temperatures will result in slower cure. Heating the assembled parts accelerates the curing process.
Activator AX-40 should be used when the temperature is less than 5°C.

Cure speed and strength vary according to the substrates. When used on mild steel components anaerobic gasket adhesives will reach full strength more rapidly than on more inert materials such as aluminium and stainless steel. EPOBOND AX-40 activator may be used to accelerate cure speed. Anaerobic adhesives only cure in the absence of air and with metal part activation.
GA-1574 is suitable for use at temperatures up to 150°C. At 130°C the bond strength will be ~25% of the strength at 21°C.
EPOBOND anaerobics retain ~90% of full strength when heated to 100°C for 90 days, then cooled and tested at 21°C.

EPOBOND anaerobics exhibit excellent chemical resistance to most oils and solvents including motor oil, leaded petrol, brake fluid, acetone, ethanol, propanol and water. Anaerobic adhesives and sealants are not recommended for use in pure oxygen or chlorine lines.

GA-1574 is not recommended on certain plastics as stress cracking can sometimes result. Some anti corrosion chemicals inhibit the cure system in this type of anaerobic. Trials are recommended to establish whether cleaning of the parts is necessary.
AX-40 Activator may be required on plated parts.
Optimal storage conditions are between 8°C and 21°C. Storage outside this temperature range can adversely affect product properties and may affect the stated shelf life.

name: UV adhesive, glass to glass and glass to metal
summary: EPOBOND UV 5253 is a single component, high viscosity adhesive formulated for bonding glass to glass and glass to metal. It cures rapidly to give a clear bond when exposed to UV-light (@365nm, see curing mechanism).
notes: Viscosity: Brookfield RVT, spindle 3, 2.5 rpm
Fixture time: glass slide fixture, 20 mW/cm² @ 365 nm
Depth of cure: cured for 30 secs @ 10 mW/cm² @ 365 nm
Tensile strength: grit blasted mild steel to glass, ASTM D2095-69
sections: EPOBOND UV 5253 is suited to applications requiring a tough cured polymer and rapid bonding. EPOBOND UV 5253 gives medium-high strength bonding of glass and glass to metal. Typical uses include glass ornaments, jewellery assembly and bonding glass furniture and displays.
Also used for gluing glass handicrafts, decorative glassware and glass display cabinets.

EPOBOND UV-curing adhesives are very sensitive to UV-light. As such, measures must be taken to protect the adhesive from exposure to UV-light from the lamp, sunlight and artificial lighting to prevent unwanted curing. The adhesives should be applied to clean, dry parts.

Ensure parts are clean, dry and free from oil and grease. Apply adhesive to one surface, bring parts together and expose the bond area to UV-light. Ensure that all of the bond is exposed. Once the adhesive is applied, the parts can be positioned correctly and then exposed to UV-light to initiate curing.

Excess adhesive can be wiped away with EPOBOND LA-70 Safety Clean or alcohol. Product can be hand applied from the bottle. Dispensing systems are also available for high volume assembly applications. Feed lines for the dispensing system must have black, UV-opaque tubing to avoid adhesive curing in the lines. Please contact your EPOBOND representative for further advice on dispensing solutions.
EPOBOND UV 5253 is designed for bonding closely fitting glass and metal parts. UV 5253 can be used to a maximum depth of ~3mm.
EPOBOND UV 5253 can be cured using sunlight. However, for a controlled, repeatable cure, UV lamps should be used.
EPOBOND UV 5253 is suitable for use at temperatures up to 130°C. At 130°C the bond strength will be ~20% of the strength at 21°C.

EPOBOND UV 5253 exhibits excellent resistance to heat ageing. Typically, exposure to heat for a prolonged period results in fully curing any uncured resin that may remain. This has the effect of increasing the bond strength when subsequently tested at 21°C.

EPOBOND UV-curing adhesives exhibit excellent chemical resistance to most oils and solvents including alcohols, methylated spirit and water. EPOBOND UV-curing adhesives are not recommended for use in pure oxygen or chlorine lines.
EPOBOND UV 5253 is formulated to cure when exposed to UV radiation of 365nm. To obtain a dry to touch finish, the adhesive should be cured in the absence of oxygen or with UV radiation of 250nm.
Optimal storage conditions are between 8°C and 21°C. Storage outside this temperature range can adversely affect product properties and may affect the stated shelf life.
